hints.title: Window Function Ranking
hints.text: Rank performance evaluations for each staff member partitioned by worker and ordered descending by date.

hints.title: Pivot Recent Ratings
hints.text: Filter to the most recent three evaluations and pivot or aggregate their scores into separate columns.

hints.title: Monotonic Strict Increase Filter
hints.text: Verify that all three scores are present and satisfy the strictly increasing condition r3 < r2 < r1.

hints.title: Reference Implementation
hints.text:
```sql
WITH ranked_reviews AS (
    SELECT 
        employee_id,
        review_date,
        rating,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY employee_id ORDER BY review_date DESC) AS rn
    FROM performance_reviews
),
recent_three AS (
    SELECT 
        employee_id,
        MAX(CASE WHEN rn = 1 THEN rating END) AS r1,
        MAX(CASE WHEN rn = 2 THEN rating END) AS r2,
        MAX(CASE WHEN rn = 3 THEN rating END) AS r3,
        COUNT(rn) AS cnt
    FROM ranked_reviews
    WHERE rn <= 3
    GROUP BY employee_id
)
SELECT 
    e.employee_id,
    e.name,
    e.department,
    r.r1 AS latest_rating
FROM recent_three r
JOIN employees e ON r.employee_id = e.employee_id
WHERE r.cnt = 3 AND r.r3 < r.r2 AND r.r2 < r.r1
ORDER BY e.employee_id ASC;
```

complexity.notes: Window partition ranking over review dates followed by condition evaluation.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Correlated three-way self joins degrade quadratically with review volume.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Window ranking filters to top 3 reviews per employee before joining employee details.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Use window functions with conditional aggregation to extract and compare recent ratings.

import pandas as pd

def find_consistently_improving_employees(employees: pd.DataFrame, performance_reviews: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    sorted_reviews = performance_reviews.sort_values(by=['employee_id', 'review_date'], ascending=[True, False])
    sorted_reviews['rn'] = sorted_reviews.groupby('employee_id').cumcount() + 1
    recent = sorted_reviews[sorted_reviews['rn'] <= 3]
    
    pivoted = recent.pivot(index='employee_id', columns='rn', values='rating').reset_index()
    if 1 not in pivoted.columns or 2 not in pivoted.columns or 3 not in pivoted.columns:
        return pd.DataFrame(columns=['employee_id', 'name', 'department', 'latest_rating'])
        
    valid = pivoted.dropna(subset=[1, 2, 3])
    improving = valid[(valid[3] < valid[2]) & (valid[2] < valid[1])]
    
    merged = improving.merge(employees, on='employee_id', how='inner')
    merged['latest_rating'] = merged[1].astype(int)
    res = merged[['employee_id', 'name', 'department', 'latest_rating']].sort_values('employee_id')
    return res
